title: CTNNB1 Genetic Variation and Its Interaction With DLK1 in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
authors: Gan, Xiaoxue; Adeerjiang, Yilinuer; Xu, Min; He, Xuan; Jiang, Sheng; Du, Guoli
journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究CTNNB1基因多态性与2型糖尿病的关联及与DLK1的分子对接，虽涉及分子对接但核心是疾病关联与湿实验验证，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: To investigate the association between Catenin Beta 1 (CTNNB1) gene polymorphisms and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), as well as the interacting molecules of CTNNB1. Bioinformatic analysis of publicly available transcriptomic datasets derived from T2DM samples identified a panel of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), among which CTNNB1 exhibited significant differential expression. Subsequent functional enrichment analysis and molecular docking revealed a co-expression network between CTNNB1 and Delta-like 1 homologue (DLK1). A total of 988 subjects including 455 patients with T2DM and 533 healthy controls were included, and the epidemiological and clinical data were collected. Association between SNPs (rs2953, rs4135387, rs1798802) of CTNNB1 and susceptibility to T2DM was analyzed. CTNNB1 expression was quantified in human serum by ELISA. A mouse model of diabetes was induced by a high-fat diet (HFD). The weight, blood glucose levels, and pancreatic morphology were detected. In a diabetes mouse model, CTNNB1 and DLK1 levels were further assessed using ELISA, Western blot, qRT-PCR, and immunohistochemistry. Immunofluorescence staining was also performed on pancreatic tissue sections to evaluate the spatial relationship within islets between beta-catenin and DLK1. Integrated analysis of DEGs and pathway enrichment identified CTNNB1 as a key gene in T2DM. Functional enrichment and molecular docking suggested that CTNNB1 and DLK1 may interact through hydrogen bonding. The CTNNB1 gene rs1798802 locus was associated with T2DM. The proportion of T2DM patients was lower in the GG genotype group than in controls (47.7% vs. 52.3%). The GG genotype of the CTNNB1 gene at the rs1798802 tended to protect the individuals from T2DM (OR = 0.640, 95% CI: 0.446-0.918, p = 0.015). Serum levels of CTNNB1 were significantly reduced in patients with T2DM (74.5 pg/mL vs. 23.78 pg/mL). Compared with control mice, HFD-induced T2DM mice showed significantly decreased protein content and gene expression of beta-catenin in the pancreatic tissue, while a concurrent decrease was also observed in DLK1 expression. Immunofluorescence staining revealed a significant overlap in the subcellular distribution of CTNNB1 and DLK1, which supported their potential physical interaction within pancreatic islet cells. The CTNNB1 gene exhibits differential expression in T2DM, and its genetic polymorphisms are also associated with the disease. The CTNNB1 gene rs1798802 loci GG genotype may be a protective factor against T2DM. CTNNB1 may interact with DLK1, potentially contributing to the regulation of pancreatic islet function. The Wnt/beta-catenin signaling pathway is inhibited in pancreatic islets in T2DM. beta-catenin (CTNNB1) is a potential target for the treatment of T2DM.
abstract_zh: 为了探讨Catenin Beta 1（CTNNB1）基因多态性与2型糖尿病（T2DM）之间的关联，以及CTNNB1的相互作用分子。对来自T2DM样本的公开转录组数据集进行生物信息学分析，鉴定出一组差异表达基因（DEGs），其中CTNNB1表现出显著的差异表达。随后的功能富集分析和分子对接揭示了CTNNB1与Delta-like 1同源物（DLK1）之间的共表达网络。共纳入988名受试者，包括455名T2DM患者和533名健康对照者，并收集了流行病学和临床数据。分析了CTNNB1的SNPs（rs2953、rs4135387、rs1798802）与T2DM易感性之间的关联。通过ELISA定量检测了人血清中CTNNB1的表达。通过高脂饮食（HFD）诱导小鼠糖尿病模型。检测了体重、血糖水平和胰腺形态。在糖尿病小鼠模型中，进一步通过ELISA、Western blot、qRT-PCR和免疫组织化学评估了CTNNB1和DLK1的水平。还对胰腺组织切片进行了免疫荧光染色，以评估胰岛内β-catenin和DLK1之间的空间关系。DEGs和通路富集的综合分析将CTNNB1鉴定为T2DM中的关键基因。功能富集和分子对接提示CTNNB1和DLK1可能通过氢键相互作用。CTNNB1基因rs1798802位点与T2DM相关。GG基因型组中T2DM患者的比例低于对照组（47.7%对52.3%）。CTNNB1基因rs1798802位点的GG基因型倾向于保护个体免受T2DM影响（OR = 0.640，95% CI：0.446-0.918，p = 0.015）。T2DM患者血清中CTNNB1水平显著降低（74.5 pg/mL对23.78 pg/mL）。与对照小鼠相比，HFD诱导的T2DM小鼠胰腺组织中β-catenin的蛋白含量和基因表达显著降低，同时DLK1表达也观察到同步下降。免疫荧光染色显示CTNNB1和DLK1在亚细胞分布上存在显著重叠，支持它们在胰岛细胞内可能发生物理相互作用。CTNNB1基因在T2DM中表现出差异表达，其遗传多态性也与该疾病相关。CTNNB1基因rs1798802位点的GG基因型可能是T2DM的保护因素。CTNNB1可能与DLK1相互作用，可能有助于调节胰岛功能。在T2DM的胰岛中，Wnt/β-catenin信号通路受到抑制。β-catenin（CTNNB1）是治疗T2DM的潜在靶点。
